summary_en: This clinical study uses photoacoustic imaging to quantify oxygen saturation in the radial arterial wall and surrounding perivascular tissue in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus. The cohort included 102 patients and 35 healthy controls. Active-disease patients showed higher measured oxygen saturation than non-active patients and controls, and the bilateral mean was associated with SLEDAI-2000 disease activity, complement levels, and serum albumin. The results support photoacoustic vascular oxygenation as a candidate non-invasive marker for SLE-related vasculitis.
